source.title: Don Vitomir Zečević: "Vaše je tijelo hram Duha Svetoga"

summary.title_hr: Don Vitomir Zečević: "Vaše je tijelo hram Duha Svetoga"
summary.abstract_hr: Don Vitomir Zečević, salezijanac i voditelj Centra za mlade Đakovačko-osječke nadbiskupije, održao je predavanje na duhovnoj obnovi za muškarce u Svetištu Božjeg milosrđa u Ovčari kod Đakova. Polazeći od riječi svetog Pavla da je tijelo hram Duha Svetoga, govori o čovjeku kao slici Božjoj, otajstvu utjelovljenja i povezanosti duhovnog i tjelesnog zdravlja. Potiče slušatelje na svakodnevnu jutarnju i večernju molitvu, ispit savjesti i predanje briga Isusu. Kritizira tetoviranje, piercing i estetske zahvate kao preoblikovanje tijela. Najviše se zadržava na čistoći i borbi protiv pornografije, za koju preporučuje filtere, post, krunicu, ispovijed i pričest.
key_points: Čovjek je vrhunac stvaranja i slika Božja, a prestaje to biti kad iz oholosti ne vrši volju Božju.
Prema predavaču, tijelo osjeća duhovno stanje čovjeka: ispovijed, molitva i klanjanje donose mir, a srdžba i mržnja štete tijelu. Navodi da većina tjelesnih bolesti dolazi od bolesti duha i duše.
Preporučuje svakodnevnu jutarnju i večernju molitvu, večernji ispit savjesti te predanje briga, loših vijesti i negativnih misli Isusu prije nego što uđu u srce.
Tetoviranje, piercing i estetske zahvate smatra unakazivanjem tijela koje nije kršćansko. Pritom se poziva na izjave egzorcista Gabriela Amortha.
Čistoća znači gledati drugu osobu bez požude, kao sestru ili majku. Sloboda nije činiti što želimo, nego ono što Bog želi.
Pornografiju opisuje kao ovisnost koja razara mozak, brakove i zdrav odnos prema spolnosti. Navodi istraživanja i statistiku o njezinim posljedicama.
Protiv pornografije predlaže filtere na mobitelu i internetu, usmjeravanje misli na vrednije stvari, post o kruhu i vodi, krunicu, ispovijed i pričest te zazivanje Duha Svetoga.
key_topics_en: the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit
man as the image of God
tattoos and reshaping of the body
key_points_en: Man is the pinnacle of creation and the image of God, and ceases to be so when, out of pride, he does not do the will of God.

According to the speaker, the body feels man's spiritual state: confession, prayer, and Eucharistic adoration bring peace, while anger and hatred harm the body. He states that most physical illnesses stem from diseases of the spirit and soul.
He recommends daily morning and evening prayer, an evening examination of conscience, and surrendering worries, bad news, and negative thoughts to Jesus before they enter the heart.
He considers tattooing, piercing, and cosmetic procedures to be a disfigurement of the body that is not Christian. In doing so, he refers to statements by exorcist Gabriel Amorth.
Purity means looking at another person without lust, as a sister or mother. Freedom is not doing what we want, but what God wants.
He describes pornography as an addiction that destroys the brain, marriages, and a healthy relationship with sexuality. He cites research and statistics on its consequences.

Against pornography, he proposes filters on mobile phones and the internet, directing thoughts toward more valuable things, fasting on bread and water, the Rosary, confession, and Holy Communion, as well as invoking the Holy Spirit.
summary.title_en: Don Vitomir Zečević: "Your Body Is a Temple of the Holy Spirit"
summary.abstract_en: Don Vitomir Zečević, a Salesian and head of the Youth Center of the Đakovo-Osijek Archdiocese, delivered a lecture at a spiritual retreat for men at the Sanctuary of Divine Mercy in Ovčara near Đakovo. Starting from the words of Saint Paul that the body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, he speaks about man as the image of God, the mystery of the Incarnation, and the connection between spiritual and physical health. He encourages listeners to engage in daily morning and evening prayer, an examination of conscience, and surrendering worries to Jesus. He criticizes tattooing, piercing, and cosmetic procedures as the reshaping of the body. He dwells the most on purity and the fight against pornography, for which he recommends filters, fasting, the Rosary, confession, and Holy Communion.
